findings.title: A thousand fewer paths to root
findings.summary_md: OpenAI published a security research post describing an autonomous pipeline that found, validated, and generated patches for 948 local privilege-escalation vulnerabilities in the Linux kernel. The run started from 2,308 candidate findings produced in 12 hours for $316,549, reproduced 1,724 vulnerabilities in 30 hours for $73,330, and screened them to 313 information-leak and 1,238 LPE candidates, at a total API cost of $1,213,430. Ten days after the scan, 61 LPEs had been patched upstream, 43 had staging patches, and 299 were being reported and discussed publicly.

findings.title: 948 Linux Root Exploits in One Run: What OpenAI's Kernel Pipeline Actually Proves - and What It Doesn't
findings.summary_md: A DEV Community analysis of OpenAI's November 4, 2026 research post summarized the funnel from 2,308 candidate findings to 948 working local privilege escalation exploits with candidate patches. It noted that 61 LPEs had been patched upstream, 43 had staging patches, and 299 were in discussion ten days after the scan, and compared the run's cost with historical bug bounties of $20,000 to $70,000 per Linux kernel LPE exploit.

findings.title: OpenAI Pipeline Finds 948 Linux Kernel Privilege Escalation Flaws
findings.summary_md: Unite.AI reported that OpenAI said on November 4, 2026 a prototype pipeline using an upcoming cyber model found and exploited 948 unique local privilege escalation vulnerabilities in Linux during a mid-October 2026 research run. The coverage described the pipeline's discovery, validation, exploitation, and patching stages and the associated API costs.

findings.title: OpenAI's pipeline found 948 Linux kernel flaws and 10 previously unknown exploit techniques in a major security study
findings.summary_md: Interesting Engineering reported that OpenAI's pipeline identified 948 distinct Linux local privilege-escalation vulnerabilities after reproducing 1,724 candidate flaws, and that researchers found at least 10 previously undocumented exploitation techniques. The article summarized the autonomous pipeline's discovery and patching results.

findings.title: OpenAI Cyber Model Uncovers 948 Linux Kernel Privilege Escalation Vulnerabilities
findings.summary_md: Cryptika reported that OpenAI said an automated research pipeline found and proved 948 separate Linux kernel privilege escalation flaws in one run. The article stated these bugs could let a normal local user gain root access.

findings.title: OpenAI's AI pipeline reproduced 1,724 Linux vulnerabilities and generated 948 working local privilege escalation exploits for $1.2 million
findings.summary_md: The Hacker News reported that OpenAI's AI pipeline reproduced 1,724 Linux vulnerabilities and generated 948 working local privilege escalation exploits for $1.2 million. It quoted OpenAI's statement that the mid-October 2026 run produced 291 information leak vulnerabilities and 948 working LPE exploits for a commonly used Linux distribution.

findings.title: OpenAI says unreleased AI model exposed 948 cyber flaws in Linux, cost $1.2 million
findings.summary_md: India Today reported that OpenAI's upcoming cyber model identified 948 cyber vulnerabilities in Linux and built exploits that could give any user root access. The article noted the total cost of the process was $1.2 million.

findings.title: Linux kernel vulnerabilities: OpenAI's AI pipeline found 948 root exploits for $1.2M
findings.summary_md: ShiftDelete reported that OpenAI said on November 4 that an automated research pipeline built on an unreleased cyber model produced 948 distinct local privilege escalation exploits. The article summarized how the pipeline worked and what it means for Linux users.
